40447-pond-and-stream.title: Pond And Stream
40447-pond-and-stream.creator: Arthur Ransome
40447-pond-and-stream.description: A book by Arthur Ransome. d the things that have happened to us there, and all the other things that you will want to know, and the things the Imp and the Elf, who are sitting side by side in my big chair, say must be told to you.

arxiv-1910-10893.title: Low-Resource Sequence Labeling via Unsupervised Multilingual Contextualized Representations
arxiv-1910-10893.creator: Zuyi Bao, Rui Huang, Chen LiKenny Q. Zhu
arxiv-1910-10893.description: Abstract Previous work on cross-lingual sequence labeling tasks either requires parallel data or bridges the two languages through word-by-word matching. Such requirements and assumptions are infeasible for most languages, especially for languages with large linguistic distances, e.g., English and Chinese.

arxiv-2107-10870.title: Multiclass versus Binary Differentially Private PAC Learning
arxiv-2107-10870.creator: Mark Bun, Marco Gaboardi, Satchit Sivakumar
arxiv-2107-10870.description: Abstract We show a generic reduction from multiclass differentially private PAC learning to binary private PAC learning. We apply this transformation to a recently proposed binary private PAC learner to obtain a private multiclass learner with sample complexity that has a polynomial dependence on the multiclass Littlestone dimension and a poly-logarithmic dependence on the number of classes.

arxiv-2111-01525.title: Non-Singular Collapse Scenario From Matter-Curvature Coupling
arxiv-2111-01525.creator: A. H. Ziaie 1 , H. Moradpour 1 , M. Mohammadi Sabet 2
arxiv-2111-01525.description: Abstract In the present work we study spherically symmetric gravitational collapse of a homogeneous perfect fluid in the context of Generalized Rastall Theory (GRT). In this modified version of the original Rastall Gravity (RG), the coupling parameter which is a representative of matter-curvature interaction is no longer a constant parameter.

arxiv-2310-19839.title: A unit of information in black hole evaporation
arxiv-2310-19839.creator: Maurice H.P.M. van Putten
arxiv-2310-19839.description: Abstract Black holes evolve by evaporation of their event horizon. While this process is believed to be unitary, there is no consensus on the recovery of information in black hole entropy. A missing link is a unit of information in black hole evaporation.

arxiv-2311-17137.title: Generative Models: What Do They Know? Do They Know Things? Let’s Find Out!
arxiv-2311-17137.creator: Xiaodan Du, Nicholas Kolkin, Gregory Shakhnarovich, Anand Bhattad
arxiv-2311-17137.description: Abstract Generative models excel at mimicking real scenes, suggesting they might inherently encode important intrinsic scene properties. In this paper, we aim to explore the following key questions: (1) What intrinsic knowledge do generative models like GANs, Autoregressive models, and Diffusion models encode?

arxiv-2405-13267.title: FLARE up your data: Diffusion-based Augmentation Method in Astronomical Imaging
arxiv-2405-13267.creator: Mohammed Talha Alam *, Raza Imam *, Mohsen Guizani, Fakhri Karray
arxiv-2405-13267.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Mohammed Talha Alam *, Raza Imam *, Mohsen Guizani, Fakhri Karray. The intersection of Astronomy and AI encounters significant challenges related to issues such as noisy backgrounds, lower resolution (LR), and the intricate process of filtering and archiving images from advanced telescopes like the James Webb. Given the dispersion of raw images in feature space, we have proposed a two-stage augmentation framework entitled as FLARE based on f eature l earning and a ugmented r esolution e nhancement.

arxiv-2408-11156.title: Dimer face polynomials in knot theory and cluster algebras
arxiv-2408-11156.creator: Karola Mészáros, Gregg Musiker, Melissa Sherman-Bennett, Alexander Vidinas
arxiv-2408-11156.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Karola Mészáros, Gregg Musiker, Melissa Sherman-Bennett, Alexander Vidinas. The set of perfect matchings of a connected bipartite plane graph G G has the structure of a distributive lattice, as shown by Propp, where the partial order is induced by the height of a matching. In this article, our focus is the dimer face polynomial of G G , which is the height generating function of all perfect matchings of G G .

arxiv-2409-01497.title: DiversityMedQA: A Benchmark for Assessing Demographic Biases in Medical Diagnosis using Large Language Models
arxiv-2409-01497.creator: Rajat Rawat, Hudson McBride, Rajarshi Ghosh, Dhiyaan Nirmal, Dhruv Alamuri, Sean O’Brien, Kevin Zhu
arxiv-2409-01497.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) gain traction in healthcare, concerns about their susceptibility to demographic biases are growing. We introduce DiversityMedQA 1 1 1 You can find the dataset here: https://huggingface.co/datasets/Rajat1212/DiversityMedQA , a novel benchmark designed to assess LLM responses to medical queries across diverse patient demographics, such as gender and ethnicity.

arxiv-2504-07895.title: Magnetic Fields of Satellite Galaxies Stronger Than Comparable Centrals in TNG100
arxiv-2504-07895.creator: Bryanne McDonough, Alexander Poulin
arxiv-2504-07895.description: Abstract Magnetic fields exist in and around galaxies, but the properties of these fields have not been fully explored due to the challenges inherent in observing and modeling them. In this Note, we explore the differences in magnetic field strength of central and satellite galaxies from the magnetohydrodynamic TNG100 simulation.

arxiv-2504-20904.title: Dual Explanations via Subgraph Matching for Malware Detection
arxiv-2504-20904.creator: Hossein Shokouhinejad, Roozbeh Razavi-Far, Griffin Higgins, Ali A. Ghorbani
arxiv-2504-20904.description: Abstract Interpretable malware detection is crucial for understanding harmful behaviors and building trust in automated security systems. Traditional explainable methods for Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) often highlight important regions within a graph but fail to associate them with known benign or malicious behavioral patterns. This limitation reduces their utility in security contexts, where alignment with verified prototypes is essential.

arxiv-2506-08096.title: A case study of translating sonifications across musical cultures for an educational application DOI: XXXXXXX.XXXXXXX Conference: Audio Mostly; June 30–July 04, 2025; Coimbra, Portugal ISBN: 978-1-4503-XXXX-X/2018/06 CCS: Human-centered computing Accessibility design and evaluation methods CCS: Appl
arxiv-2506-08096.creator: Chris M. Harrison, James W. Trayford, Arron George, Leigh Harrison, Rubén García-Benito, Shirin Haque, Rose Shepherd
arxiv-2506-08096.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Chris M. Harrison, James W. Trayford, Arron George, Leigh Harrison, Rubén García-Benito, Shirin Haque, Rose Shepherd. Sonification can be part of educational resources that can be accessible to those who prefer, or require, non-visual learning methods. Furthermore, sonification can contribute to an engaging multi-sensory learning experience, which are known to benefit general learners. Whilst some sonification can be relatively agnostic to musical culture, many sonifications are subject to culturally influenced choices, such as the chosen harmonies, rhythmic structures, and instrumentation.

arxiv-2506-09600.title: Effective Red-Teaming of Policy-Adherent Agents
arxiv-2506-09600.creator: Itay Nakash, George Kour, Koren Lazar, Matan Vetzler, Guy Uziel, Ateret Anaby-Tavor
arxiv-2506-09600.description: Abstract Task-oriented LLM-based agents are increasingly used in domains with strict policies, such as refund eligibility or cancellation rules. The challenge lies in ensuring that the agent consistently adheres to these rules and policies, appropriately refusing any request that would violate them, while still maintaining a helpful and natural interaction.

arxiv-2508-08429.title: Improving Facial Rig Semantics for Tracking and Retargeting 251
arxiv-2508-08429.creator: Dalton Omens, Allise Thurman, Jihun Yu, Ronald Fedkiw
arxiv-2508-08429.description: Abstract . In this paper, we consider retargeting a tracked facial performance to either another person or to a virtual character in a game or virtual reality (VR) environment. We remove the difficulties associated with identifying and retargeting the semantics of one rig framework to another by utilizing the same framework (3DMM, FLAME, MetaHuman, etc.) for both subjects.

europmc-pmc4726722.title: The emerging role of Nrf2 in mitochondrial function.
europmc-pmc4726722.creator: Dinkova-Kostova AT, Abramov AY.
europmc-pmc4726722.description: The transcription factor NF-E2 p45-related factor 2 (Nrf2; gene name NFE2L2) allows adaptation and survival under conditions of stress by regulating the gene expression of diverse networks of cytoprotective proteins, including antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and detoxification...

plos-pone-0011196.title: Diagnostic Accuracy and Optimal Use of Three Tests for Tuberculosis in Live Badgers
plos-pone-0011196.creator: Julian A. Drewe, Alexandra J. Tomlinson, Neil J. Walker et al.
plos-pone-0011196.description: PLOS ONE research article. Accurate diagnosis of tuberculosis (TB) due to infection with Mycobacterium bovis is notoriously difficult in live animals, yet important if we are to understand the epidemiology of TB and devise effective strategies to limit its spread. Currently available tests for diagnosing T

pmc-10509200.title: Ligament injury in adult zebrafish triggers ECM remodeling and cell dedifferentiation for scar-free regeneration
pmc-10509200.creator: Troy Anderson, Julia Mo, Ernesto Gagarin, Desmarie Sherwood, Maria Blumenkrantz, Eric Mao, Gianna Leon, Hailey Levitz, Hung-Jhen Chen, Kuo-Chang Tseng, Peter Fabian, J Gage Crump, Joanna Smeeton
pmc-10509200.description: After traumatic injury, healing of mammalian ligaments is typically associated with fibrotic scarring as opposed to scar-free regeneration. In contrast, here we show that the ligament supporting the jaw joint of adult zebrafish is capable of rapid and complete scar-free healing.

pmc-10669302.title: Muscle Involvement in Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis: Understanding the Pathogenesis and Advancing Therapeutics
pmc-10669302.creator: Elisa Duranti, Chiara Villa, Tatiana L Nemirovskaya, Tatiana Kostrominova
pmc-10669302.description: Amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) is a fatal condition characterized by the selective loss of motor neurons in the motor cortex, brainstem, and spinal cord. Muscle involvement, muscle atrophy, and subsequent paralysis are among the main features of this disease, which is defined as a neuromuscular disorder.

pmc-11465837.title: Technology‐based instrumental activities of daily living in persons with Alzheimer's disease and related disorders
pmc-11465837.creator: Jared F Benge, Arsh Ali, Neha Chandna, Noor Rana, Rachel Mis, David A González, Andrew M Kiselica, Michael K Scullin, Robin C Hilsabeck
pmc-11465837.description: INTRODUCTIONInstrumental activities of daily living (iADLs) increasingly involve technology (e.g., making payments online, texting). The current study examined the applicability and diagnostic accuracy of technology‐based iADLs in those evaluated for Alzheimer's disease and related dementias (ADRD).METHODSA total of 264 care partners of persons undergoing comprehensive interdisciplinary evaluations completed the Functional Activities Questionnaire and 11 technology‐based iADL items.

pmc-11645020.title: MAARS: Multiagent Actor–Critic Approach for Resource Allocation and Network Slicing in Multiaccess Edge Computing
pmc-11645020.creator: Ducsun Lim, Inwhee Joe, Hai Dong
pmc-11645020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). This paper presents a novel algorithm to address resource allocation and network-slicing challenges in multiaccess edge computing (MEC) networks. Network slicing divides a physical network into virtual slices, each tailored to efficiently allocate resources and meet diverse service requirements. To maximize the completion rate of user-computing tasks within these slices, the problem is decomposed into two subproblems: efficient core-to-edge slicing (ECS) and autonomous resource slicing (ARS).

pmc-12575357.title: Proteins linked to type II interferon response in Sjögren’s disease: novel indicators for disease monitoring and predicting treatment response to leflunomide and hydroxychloroquine combination therapy
pmc-12575357.creator: Wing-Yi Wong, Helen L. Leavis, Sofie L. M. Blokland, Valentin M. D. Baloche, Joel A. G. van Roon
pmc-12575357.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). ObjectiveTo identify biomarkers and endotypes predictive of treatment response, monitor disease activity, and explore pathways associated with the clinical efficacy of leflunomide and hydroxychloroquine combination therapy (LEF/HCQ) in patients with primary Sjögren’s disease (SjD).MethodsSerum proteome (Olink Immuno-oncology panel, analyzing 92 proteins) of 29 patients with SjD of the RepurpSS-I study and 8 healthy controls was analyzed at baseline and after 24 weeks of LEF/HCQ. Proteomic changes were correlated to standard and novel clinical endpoints.

pmc-12716976.title: Collapsing Sparse Responses in Likert-Type Scale Data: Advantages and Disadvantages for Model Fit in CFA
pmc-12716976.creator: Jin Liu, Yu Bao, Christine DiStefano, Wei Jiang
pmc-12716976.description: Applied researchers often encounter situations where certain item response categories receive very few endorsements, resulting in sparse data. Collapsing categories may mitigate sparsity by increasing cell counts, yet the methodological consequences of this practice remain insufficiently explored. The current study examined the effects of response collapsing in Likert-type scale data through a simulation study under the confirmatory factor analysis model.

pmc-13265561.title: Identification and functional characterization of plasma exosomal miR-618 as a novel biomarker in recurrent depressive disorder
pmc-13265561.creator: Xiangyang Zhang, Binbin Chen, Xue Yi, Meitao Duan, Chen Wang, Shuxian Li, Wei Wei
pmc-13265561.description: BackgroundGiven the substantial clinical and financial burden of Recurrent Depressive Disorder (RDD) and the critical lack of reliable biomarkers, this study investigated plasma exosomal microRNA (miRNA) as candidate biomarkers and therapeutic targets to overcome reliance on subjective diagnosis. The pathogenesis of RDD remains incompletely understood.

pmc-13412802.title: Exogenous Hormones and Their Clinical Implications for the Development and Growth of Meningioma Tumours
pmc-13412802.creator: Holly Roy, Marios Stavrakas, Samiul Muquit
pmc-13412802.description: Meningiomas are the most common central nervous system tumour and are associated with significant morbidity. Mounting evidence implicates the role of exogenous hormones in meningioma development and growth. This has led to increasing pressure on healthcare professionals to understand the risk profile of different hormonal compounds with regards to meningioma incidence and growth.

pmc-13427068.title: Wearable Devices for Monitoring and Management of Comorbid Obstructive Sleep Apnea and Hypertension: Scoping Review
pmc-13427068.creator: Hongyi Wang, Anran Cheng, Yusheng Li, Haining Zhang, Shun Fan, Rong Shen, Wei Zhang, Huanan Li, Jingui Wang

pmc-13605215.title: Factors Associated with Clinically Inadequate Bowel Preparation Among Patients with Diabetes Mellitus Undergoing Colonoscopy: A Single-Center Observational Study
pmc-13605215.creator: Ivana Jukić, Duje Denona, Tina Bečić, Ajka Pribisalić, Josipa Radić, Mislav Radić, Damir Fabijanić, Vedran Kovačić, Jonatan Vuković
pmc-13605215.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Background: Adequate bowel preparation is essential for high-quality colonoscopy, yet patients with diabetes mellitus remain particularly vulnerable to suboptimal cleansing. This study evaluated factors associated with clinically inadequate cleansing among patients with diabetes mellitus undergoing colonoscopy. Methods: This ambispective observational study included 194 adult patients with diabetes mellitus who underwent total colonoscopy at University Hospital Center Split between 1 January 2019 and 30 October 2025 and were prepared using an institutional split-dose PEG/macrogol-based bowel preparation approach.
